title: Distributed Topological Charge and Spinorial Holonomy in Yukawa-Regularized Graphene Disclinations
authors: A. M. de M. Carvalho, G. Q. Garcia, E. Brito, C. Furtado
abstract: Conical geometries provide the standard description of disclinations, but they concentrate the curvature at a singular apex. We introduce a Yukawa-type regularization that replaces this singularity by a smooth curvature distribution while preserving the asymptotic topology of the defect. Exact expressions are obtained for the conformal factor, curvature, and enclosed topological charge. The resulting geometry exhibits a scale-dependent topological charge and a corresponding radius-dependent holonomy, establishing a direct connection between distributed curvature and geometric phases. We further investigate the dynamics of massless Dirac quasiparticles in this background and show that the regularized core modifies the spin connection while preserving the asymptotic topological signature of the defect. These results provide a finite-core extension of the conventional conical description and offer a natural framework for studying geometric and topological effects in graphene-like systems.
summary: This paper regularizes the singular geometry of disclinations in graphene using a Yukawa potential, creating a smooth, finite-core defect structure. It calculates that this regularization leads to scale-dependent topological charge and a smoothly varying spinorial holonomy for Dirac quasiparticles. This provides a physically realistic extension beyond idealized models for studying geometric phases in 2D materials.
main_problem: The study addresses the singularity inherent in ideal conical geometries used to model topological defects (disclinations) by introducing a smooth, finite-core regularization.
main_result: The Yukawa regularization successfully replaces the singular curvature with a distributed source, leading to scale-dependent topological charge and a smoothly varying, radius-dependent spinorial holonomy for quasiparticles.
method: The authors solve differential equations derived from geometric considerations (Poisson-like equation) using a modified Helmholtz kernel to model the curvature distribution.
model_or_system: The system models graphene-like materials containing topological disclinations. The physics is described by massless Dirac quasiparticles propagating in a curved background metric determined by the Yukawa regularization.
key_observables: Scale-dependent topological charge, radius-dependent holonomy (geometric phase), and the conformal factor $\Omega(r)$.
important_parameters: The screening length ($\ell = \mu^{-1}$) controls the size of the finite core; $\Lambda$ characterizes the total integrated curvature.
main_assumptions: Ideal conical defects are insufficient due to singularities, necessitating a Yukawa-type regularization that preserves asymptotic topology.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the normalized enclosed topological charge $Q(ho)/\Lambda$ versus radial coordinate $ho$, showing a monotonic increase from zero at the core to the total value $\Lambda$ asymptotically.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the need for regularization, deriving the smooth metric components using the Yukawa kernel, and finally analyzing the resulting dynamics of Dirac quasiparticles in this modified background.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete mathematical framework for handling singular topological defects in condensed matter systems, offering insights into how finite-size effects modify global geometric phases relevant to quantum transport.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Conformal factor Ω(r) (core-regular gauge, Ω(0) = 0) as a function of r (logarithmic scale) for several values of the regularization parameter µ.
FIG. 2. Scalar curvature R(r) given by Eq. (4.2) as a function of the radial coordinate r (logarithmic scale) for the same set of µ values used in Fig. 1.

FIG. 3. Normalized enclosed topological charge Q(ρ)/Λ as a function of the radial coordinate ρ for different values of the screening parameter µ. The charge increases monotonically from zero at the regular core to the asymptotic value Q(ρ) = Λ. Larger values of µ localize the curvature more strongly and lead to a faster saturation of the enclosed topological charge. The horizontal dashed lines indicate representative fractions of the total charge associated with the discrete holonomy-invariance condition discussed in Sec. V.
